NutriFresh Foods - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Foods Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Foods' Q2 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer; and Jordan Lee, Chief Growth Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q2 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, capital expenditure plans and priorities, updates on M&A activity and portfolio management, and key achievements and challenges in the quarter.

First, regarding e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue. As we examine our segment performance, e-commerce stands out as one of our fastest-growing channels. This quarter, e-commerce sales surged 48% year-over-year to $216 million, accounting for 18% of our total net revenue of $1.2 billion—rising from 12% in Q2 2023 and 15% sequentially from Q1. This continues a streak of six straight quarters of double-digit acceleration, surpassing our overall company growth of 8% year-over-year and highlighting the structural shift we're leveraging in the Food & Beverage sector.

To provide context, our e-commerce gross merchandise value reached $285 million, propelled by a 32% rise in average order value to $68, driven by personalized bundling of high-margin offerings like NutriFresh Protein Shakes and our new plant-based snack packs. Basket sizes grew 15% as customers added complementary products, such as zero-sugar electrolyte beverages with ready-to-eat meal kits, similar to trends at peers like PepsiCo's PantryShop direct-to-consumer platform.

Regionally, North America dominates, comprising 72% of e-commerce sales at $155 million, up 55% year-over-year. Partnerships with Instacart and Amazon Fresh have transformed this, lifting same-day delivery to 28% of orders—comparable to Kroger's Boost model—and cutting customer acquisition costs by 22% via targeted ads on TikTok Shop. In APAC, growth exploded 75% to $42 million, powered by Tmall and Shopee integrations in China and Southeast Asia, where urban millennials are embracing our low-calorie kombucha amid post-COVID health trends. Europe grew more modestly at 12% to $19 million, hampered by strict EU regulations on single-use plastics, but our recycled-material shippers have boosted fulfillment Net Promoter Scores by 18 points.

Fueling this momentum are year-to-date investments exceeding $45 million in tech solutions addressing F&B perishable logistics. Our proprietary AI-driven demand forecasting, powered by Snowflake and Shopify Plus, has reduced stockouts by 40% and improved cold-chain inventory turns to 12 times annually—essential for freshness in products like Greek yogurt parfaits. We've introduced a subscription model inspired by HelloFresh, now boasting 450,000 subscribers that generate 35% recurring revenue and lifetime values over $450, supported by 85% retention through predictive churn analytics. Backend micro-fulfillment centers in hubs like Chicago and Singapore have lowered last-mile costs to 9% of GMV from 14% last year, sustaining e-commerce gross margins at 42% against 38% company-wide.

Strategically, e-commerce is transforming our omnichannel strategy. Combining direct-to-consumer with retailer platforms like ShopRite and Whole Foods digital shelves, we're securing 25% incremental volume from non-traditional shoppers. This is crucial in F&B amid private-label pressures from Aldi and Lidl squeezing CPG margins; our DTC channel provides five times the consumer preference data, guiding R&D for successes like keto-friendly energy bars. We anticipate e-commerce reaching 22% of revenue by fiscal 2025, with Q3 growth guided at 50-55%, bolstered by Black Friday initiatives and Flipkart expansion in India. Risks like freight volatility and APAC tariff hikes are mitigated by hedging and nearshoring to Mexico.

In essence, e-commerce drives profitable scale, adding 150 basis points to operating margin expansion this quarter. We're building a defensible moat through F&B-tailored innovation, not just chasing volume.

Second, concerning capital expenditure plans and priorities. As we conclude our Q2 results discussion, our capital expenditure outlook for fiscal 2024 and beyond underpins our strategy for sustainable growth in this evolving Food & Beverage environment. We're targeting total Capex of $475 million this year, up 12% from $425 million in fiscal 2023, balancing maintenance, growth, and innovation against commodity pressures like 25% year-over-year cocoa spikes and sugar fluctuations.

Breaking it down by priorities aligned with supply chain resilience, portfolio premiumization, and sustainability leadership—where we're generating superior ROI versus peers like PepsiCo and Mondelez.

Maintenance and efficiency Capex claims 35%, or about $166 million, to optimize our 45 global manufacturing facilities. This includes $80 million for automation like robotic palletizers and high-speed fillers akin to Nestlé's OptiLine. North America gets 45% or $75 million, retrofitting our Chicago flagship with Siemens AI predictive maintenance for 15-20% less downtime and $12 million annual savings by fiscal 2025. Europe receives 25% or $42 million for EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation compliance via modular conveyors reducing waste.

Capacity expansion is our biggest slice at 40% or $190 million, responding to demand for functional beverages and plant-based snacks—U.S. RTD tea up 8% per IRI, global plant-based dairy alternatives at 12% CAGR through 2028 per Euromonitor. We're spending $95 million on two new aseptic lines in Southeast Asia—$60 million in Vietnam, $35 million in Indonesia—for low-sugar kombucha, aiming for 25% volume growth in the $2.5 billion APAC functional beverage market. This leverages local sourcing with 70% forward contracts at 10% below spot. In the Americas, $65 million builds a greenfield snack facility in Mexico for 50,000 tons of air-fried potato crisps, countering 15% logistics inflation, with 18-22% IRR and 24-month breakeven.

Innovation and digital transformation take 15% or $71 million. $40 million funds R&D in California and Singapore for precision fermentation like Perfect Day's alt-milk proteins, suited to our aseptic bottling. This encompasses $15 million for IBM Food Trust blockchain pilots for organic juices amid ESG focus. $20 million upgrades to SAP S/4HANA integrate Nielsen scans and weather data for 10% better forecast accuracy and $25 million working capital savings.

Sustainability gets 10% or $48 million, up 30% year-over-year. Facing Scope 3 scrutiny post-ISSB, $25 million installs solar microgrids at five plants in water-stressed India and Brazil for 30% renewables by fiscal 2026—matching Danone's goals with 3-year payback via incentives. APAC allocates 40% or $19 million to regenerative agriculture with Indonesian cocoa farmers, cutting chocolate snack carbon by 12%.

Overall, Capex targets high-ROI projects with 2.5-year blended payback, 60% operations-funded, 40% low-cost 4.2% debt. We're halting non-core spend like vending amid 7-9% food-at-home inflation. Fiscal 2025 could rise to $500-525 million if RTD margins exceed 28%, gaining 150 basis points premium share.

Third, in terms of updates on M&A activity and portfolio management. Progress here is core to our high-quality growth strategy in Food & Beverage. NutriFresh Foods adheres to disciplined capital allocation, pursuing bolt-on acquisitions in functional beverages, plant-based proteins, and premium snacks, while pruning underperformers—outshining peers like PepsiCo's premiumization or Mondelez's snacking amid cocoa up 25% YTD and palm oil 15% above pre-pandemic.

In Q2, we completed the $450 million acquisition of VitalRoots Nutrition, a California leader in plant-based protein bars and RTD shakes with 12% U.S. clean-label protein share, where demand rose 18% per Nielsen. Accretive to EPS at 10.5x trailing EBITDA—below 13x sector average—we forecast $65 million run-rate synergies by 2025 end: $35 million procurement via our supply chain, $30 million SG&A from shared marketing and 150,000-point North American distribution at Walmart and Kroger.

Integration exceeds plan. We've cut 20% of VitalRoots SKUs, focusing on RootFuel bars up 22% in Q3 via e-commerce, now 35% of sales from 25%. Our AgriPredict AI forecasting boosts inventory turns 15%, mirroring legacy gains amid nut price swings.

Our pipeline holds $1.2 billion in value, meeting 15%+ EBITDA margins, 8-10% organic growth, ESG fit. We're eyeing a €200 million EMEA tuck-in for kombucha/adaptogens like GT's, entering €5 billion European functional drinks at 14% CAGR, platforming FlavorForge extensions. Announcement possible year-end, funded by $800 million liquidity and $1.5 billion revolver.

On portfolio, our multi-year program unlocked $250 million value. Q2 divested Midwest Creamery dairy for $180 million cash—4% revenue, 2% EBITDA, hit by 10% milk volatility and 5% U.S. fluid milk decline per USDA. Sold at 1.2x book, deleveraging net debt/EBITDA to 2.1x.

Proceeds boost premium health segments—now 72% portfolio from 55% two years ago. Plant-based including VitalRoots and GreenPulse oat milk grew 19% organically vs. 11% category. Snacks premiumized: CrunchVita clusters up 25% APAC via 7-Eleven, Tmall e-com at 28%.

North America (58% revenue) leads via M&A, protein share to 9% vs. Kellogg's 7%, margins +220 bps to 28% on blockchain pea protein traceability.

EMEA (22%) sharpens on sustainable beverages post cordial divestiture; AquaVive sparkling water +16% on 12% low-cal demand per Kantar, local sourcing counters Brexit duties.

APAC (15%), +14% YoY on urbanization; scouting Japanese matcha RTDs for ¥1.2 trillion market at 9% CAGR, dual-sourcing holds 98% service amid China disruptions.

Latin America (5%) simplifies SKUs 15% vs. 20% inflation, eyes quinoa snacks.

Forward, this drives 7-9% FY24 organic growth, ROIC to 14% from 12.5%, 4-6 accretive deals at <11x, $1.1 billion FCF, A- rating. It's consumer-centric resilience like Nestlé and Unilever.

Finally, looking at key achievements and challenges in the quarter. As we reflect on Q2 2024, our performance was shaped by notable wins and hurdles across Beverages, Snacks, and Health & Nutrition segments, with regional nuances and strategic actions. We posted net revenues of $1.2 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year or 9.1% organic constant-currency. Adjusted EBITDA hit $179 million, up 12%, margins +110 bps to 14.9%.

On achievements, top-line strength came from 3.5% global organic volume—strongest in three quarters—via 5.2% Beverages, 4.1% Snacks; Health & Nutrition flat volume but 11% pricing growth. Premiumization shone: VitaGlow functional beverages and ProteinCrunch bars added $75 million incremental sales, 2.2 points growth.

North America excelled at 10.4% organic, gaining 120 bps CSD share vs. Coca-Cola/PepsiCo via Zero Sugar Revolution; FizzVita Zero +28%, 15,000 more Walmart/Kroger doors. Snacks gained from Q1 MexiCrunch acquisition: $40 million revenue, 200 bps margin via synergies.

EMEA +6.8% despite sentiment, UK/Germany +12% GreenBite plant-based; 15 reduced-sodium SKUs took 3% savory share per Nielsen. APAC +8.2%, India/SEA RTD VitaZen +35% on Flipkart/Shopee. LATAM +5.1%, Brazil energy drinks +22% soccer-driven.

Operationally, gross margins +180 bps to 38.2% on $20 million Supply Chain 2.0 savings: hedged 85% Q3 cocoa at $4,200/ton below spot, Maersk freight -15%, SAP IBP AI at 70% plants cut inventory 12%/$12 million, forecasts 92% accurate.

Sustainability: 25% recycled PET ahead of 2025, saved $5 million resin, NPS +8 to 65.

Strategically, e-commerce 18% sales +25% Amazon/D2C; $20 million precision fermentation with Perfect Day for Q4 dairy-free creamers in $6 billion alt-dairy at 14% CAGR.

Challenges included 4.2% COGS inflation: Brazil sugar +22% El Niño, cocoa +45% to $10,000/ton West Africa shortages like Hershey/Mondelez; passed 70% pricing, absorbed $10 million Snacks.

Downtrading hit mass CSD -2% to private labels per IRI, EMEA UK -1.5% cost-of-living like Unilever. FX -$6 million USD strength APAC. Supply snarls: LA port +10 days Indonesian flavors, idled CA plants $3 million; Midwest labor/avian flu egg -15%, overtime +18%.

Regulatory: CA Prop 12 pork $2 million, EU Nutri-Score risks 10% chocolate; $8 million R&D for A/B reformulations.

Competition: Keurig Dr Pepper RTD coffee pricing -50 bps energy share US, Nestlé Vital Proteins health claims hit collagen.

These validate Health-Powered Growth: 60% launches functional gut/immunity in $200 billion trend. Rationalizing 20% low-margin SKUs for 16% FY24 EBITDA. Hedging/Guatemala coffee farm secures 30% beans; Thailand plant APAC, DoorDash omnichannel North America.

Q2 shows resilience: volume/margin growth, ESG progress on track for 7-9% organic, 15%+ EBITDA FY.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Rachel Kim to provide more detail on our financial results.

Rachel Kim (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q2 2024. Net sales were $1.2 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38%, impacted by elevated input costs from commodities like cocoa and sugar. Operating income was $150 million, and earnings per share were $0.92. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $800 million in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 7-9% organic revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA growth of 12-15%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Jennifer Wong with Citi. Please proceed.

Jennifer Wong (Citi):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Good morning, Jennifer. Inflation continues to be a key pressure, with cocoa prices up 25% year-over-year, sugar volatility from events like El Niño in Brazil adding 22%, and broader 4.2% COGS inflation. We've hedged 85% of Q3 cocoa needs below spot and passed through about 70% via targeted pricing, absorbing some in Snacks to safeguard volumes. Our supply chain efficiencies, like AI demand sensing and forward contracts, helped expand gross margins 180 basis points despite this. We're staying agile with dynamic hedging and vertical integration, such as our Guatemala coffee investments, to protect profitability.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Bank of America. Please proceed.

Robert Kline (Bank of America):
What are your plans for the new plant-based protein shakes and what is the expected impact on growth?

Jordan Lee (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Robert. Our new plant-based protein shakes, integrated from the VitalRoots acquisition and our own R&D, are central to premiumization. We've rationalized SKUs to focus on high-velocity RootFuel-inspired variants, bundling them with e-commerce subscriptions for higher AOV. Plans include expanding distribution to 20,000 more doors via Walmart and Kroger partnerships, plus APAC e-com pilots on Tmall. We expect 20-25% volume growth in the category, contributing $50-60 million incremental revenue in FY24, with immediate EPS accretion and 15%+ EBITDA margins, boosting overall organic growth by 1-2 points while enhancing our health & nutrition portfolio share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with Deutsche Bank. Please proceed.

Priya Patel (Deutsche Bank):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Tom Herrera (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Priya, thanks for the question. Disruptions like LA port congestion adding 10 days for Indonesian flavors, Midwest avian flu cutting egg supply 15%, and China zero-COVID echoes persist, but we've built resilience. Our AI forecasting on Snowflake/SAP IBP cut stockouts 40%, inventory 12%, with 12x cold-chain turns. Micro-fulfillment in Chicago/Singapore slashed last-mile to 9% GMV, Maersk partnerships reduced ocean freight 15%, and nearshoring to Mexico/Vietnam offsets logistics inflation. Service levels hold at 98%, supporting 3.5% volume growth. We're also advancing blockchain with IBM for traceability, positioning us ahead on ESG and efficiency.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Laura Chen with UBS. Please proceed.

Laura Chen (UBS):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Rachel Kim (CFO):
Laura, our outlook remains constructive. We're on track for full-year 7-9% organic growth and 12-15% adjusted EBITDA expansion. Q3 e-commerce should grow 50-55%, Capex at $475 million focused on high-ROI capacity like SEA aseptic lines and Mexico snacks. M&A pipeline supports 4-6 deals, portfolio now 72% premium. Inflation headwinds are managed via 70%+ hedging and pricing discipline, supply chain at peak efficiency. Risks like FX and tariffs are hedged; we're confident in executing for shareholder value.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Thompson for closing remarks.

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriFresh Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
